thread:
Alex: Heads-up — following the RFC, I sketched a proposed set of canary heuristics for air-gapped upgrades. Wanted quick feedback before I formalize.
Mira: pinging the ops crew. do we want canaries at the node level or pool level? :thinking:
Sam: pool-level seems safer for air-gapped since individual nodes might be flaky due to local infra.
Jen: agree. pool-level gives clearer blast radius. but how do we detect a bad bundle in an isolated site? we need metrics that don't rely on external telemetry.
Alex: good point. proposal: healthcheck + request-success-rate + CPU/kvm mem spikes over a 5min window. thresholds: fail if success_rate < 98% or error_rate delta > 0.5% vs baseline.
Kai: can we compute baseline pre-upgrade? we can snapshot 1h of metrics before rollout and use that as baseline.
Mira: baseline + anomaly windows makes sense. also include a checksum verification step right after install and before process start — ensures packaging corruption caught early.
Sam: what about heuristics for slow regressions? some perf regressions won't show in 5min.
Alex: plan: stage 0 -> 1hr smoke (basic health), stage 1 -> 24hr canary at 5% capacity, stage 2 -> 50% for 24hr, then full. each stage has gating checks: smoke OK, baseline perf w/in 5%, error_rate w/in 0.5%, cpu mem w/in 10%.
Jen: how do teams rollback in air-gapped sites? can't just fetch previous image from cloud.
Kai: we must include the previous bundle in the manifest (store last N bundles locally). the bootstrap loader should allow explicit --force-bundle <id> to revert.
Mira: need signing policy: only signed bundles can be deployed, and rolling back requires either signed rollback bundle or a signed admin override key action (HSM).
Sam: can the canary stage auto-fail and trigger rollback? yes/no?
Alex: yes, auto-fail for critical checks. but require two independent failing checks to auto-rollback to avoid flapping.
Jen: what about partial rollbacks? e.g., revert only control-plane vs data-plane components.
Kai: package is layered. we can mark components as independent artifacts in the bundle manifest and allow per-component rollbacks. but that increases complexity and test surface.
Mira: tradeoff: smaller rollback grain reduces impact area but increases combinatorial testing. maybe start with whole-bundle rollback and add component-level later.
Sam: test plan? we should simulate degraded network and disk corruption to ensure health checks detect issues.
Alex: agree. add chaos scenarios: dropped packets, delayed DNS, limited disk IO, corrupted delta patch. run them in our onprem test harness.
deploy-bot: deploy-job created: job/upgrade-canary-sim-1792345678 queued (env: staging-onprem). Logs: https://fake-ci/jobs/1792345678
Jen: ops runbook draft: 1) monitor canary dashboard, 2) if gating metrics breach -> trigger rollback via admin CLI: redwoodctl rollback --bundle <id> --reason "auto" 3) if rollback fails, follow manual recovery steps (boot from rescue image).
Kai: add steps to rotate keys after any signed-bundle compromise. we should treat a compromised bundle like a security incident.
Mira: ok, I'll update the RFC with: pool-level canary, baseline snapshot, staged rollout (1hr smoke, 24/24/100), dual-check rollback trigger, include previous N bundles locally, signing + HSM override, whole-bundle rollback initially, chaos tests. any objections?
Sam: no objections. add a note about storage size for keeping N bundles and cleanup policy.
Alex: thanks — I'll update and send for review. small follow-up: can we add a throttle for rollback frequency (e.g., limit 1 rollback per site per 6hr) to avoid thrash?
Jen: yes add cooldown; also log an event to central telemetry for audit.
Mira: will add cooldown and audit event in RFC. moving to PR after edits. :thumbsup:
